subject: Billing drift after 09/14 incident — reconciliation, evidence, and credit authorization
messages:
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@olive-tech.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@olive-tech.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexplained billing drift after 09/14 incident

Hi Mateo,

We're seeing a large unexplained jump on our September invoices starting on 2025-09-14 (around 00:30 UTC). Per our normal usage the week of Sep 7–13 we average ~120k tokens/day, but Sep 14–16 shows multiple days with ~360k tokens/day. Attached is a CSV export from our billing portal (usage_export_sep10-16.csv).

Can you confirm if this is related to the incident you posted on the status page last week? If this maps to an internal retry/replay on Redwood's side we will expect a credit for the overage. Please let me know what evidence you can provide (request ids, server logs, incident window) and the next steps to get a corrective credit applied.

Invoice references: INV-OLV-20250914 and INV-OLV-20250915.

Thanks,
Tim Jenkins
Head of Platform
Olive Tech
attachments: usage_export_sep10-16.csv (CSV)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unexplained billing drift after 09/14 incident

Hi Tim — thanks for the flag and for attaching the CSV.

Short answer: we are investigating now and I will own the coordination. Initial steps we are taking:
- Engineering will correlate your request_ids to our ingestion/serving logs for 2025-09-14 00:00–06:00 UTC.
- We will produce a short evidence bundle (request ids, internal replay metric, and incident timeline) you can share with procurement.
- Customer success will prepare a provisional credit calculation; finance will need to sign-off on amounts > $5k.

Monica (cc) — please confirm we have the correct invoices and whether Olive already has an outstanding credit note. Karthik — can you run an expedited log correlation for the session window and include any signs of repeated KV-cache replays or session re-entrancy?

I’ll follow up with a proposed credit by EOD tomorrow (Thu). If you prefer, we can pause invoice collection for the disputed dates while we reconcile — let me know.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Success Manager

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Hi Tim — thanks for sending the CSV and invoice ids. I pulled INV-OLV-20250914/15 — those are the invoices we would adjust if corrective credits are approved.

Quick ask: for credits that exceed $5,000 we require an authorized signature (DocuSign) from the billing contact. If you can confirm the right signatory (name and email) I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope once finance confirms the provisional amount.

Also: could you confirm whether any of the token volume listed in the CSV is from repeated session replays on your side (e.g., automated job resubmits)? That helps us separate client-side retries from server-side duplication.

Regards,
Monica
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Unexplained billing drift after 09/14 incident

Mateo / Monica — quick technical summary from infra:

> On 2025-09-14 at ~00:27 UTC a routing change triggered a short window where ephemeral workers rehydrated previously cached KV states for a subset (~0.7%) of sessions. That rehydration path had a logic bug that caused repeated cache playback for the same session key during prefix population. In the logs this appears as repeated generation calls tied to identical request_id prefixes; the effect multiplies token accounting by the number of replays (we observed up to 3x for affected sessions).
>
> We have a list of request_id prefixes and a start/end window (2025-09-14T00:26:47Z–2025-09-14T00:41:12Z).

Proposed customer-facing approach:
- Produce an evidence bundle (list of request_ids, server-side replay count per request_id, timestamped logs).
- Compute an overage by subtracting the single-run token estimate from the replayed total (i.e., credit only duplicated tokens).
- Offer a provisional credit and apply as a negative line on the Sep invoices; finalize after finance sign-off and DocuSign if required.

Estimate: for Olive Tech we calculate ~228k duplicated tokens across the incident window (matches entries Tim sent). At our published rate that maps to a provisional credit of ~$3,420. Finance will need to confirm final rounding and tax handling.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing credit approval (Olive Tech)

Thanks — finance reviewed Karthik's numbers and we provisionally approve a credit of $3,420.00 net.

Action required:
- Mateo: please send the DocuSign envelope to Tim's billing contact for approval (we need sign-off for audit when credit > $1,000).
- Once signed, finance will apply the credit to INV-OLV-20250914 and INV-OLV-20250915 and reflect the negative line on the customer portal.

I attached a proposed credit note we will post after signature.

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing drift after 09/14 incident — reconciliation, evidence, and credit authorization

Tim — quick update and closing notes.

1) Evidence bundle: attached is a short incident summary and the list of request_id prefixes we used to reconcile your CSV (redwood_postincident_summary_20250914.txt). That includes the server-side replay counts and the exact window. You can also view the full postmortem here: https://app.redwood.com/postmortems/RW-20250914-kv-replay

2) Credit: Laura confirmed a provisional credit of $3,420.00. I have sent the DocuSign envelope to the billing contact you provided (tim.billing@olive-tech.com). Once signed, finance will apply the negative line to INV-OLV-20250914 and INV-OLV-20250915; you should see it reflected on the portal within 48 hours of signature.

3) Mitigation: engineering has deployed a patch that prevents the cache rehydration replay path from re-entering prefix population. We also added an internal guard metric that will alert at 1.5x session token deltas.

4) Next steps for us:
- Monica will confirm portal visibility and close the support case post-credit.
- Karthik will retain the reconciliation artifacts for audit (48 months).

Appreciate the patience and apologies for the disruption. If you need a formal letter of remediation for your procurement team we can produce that as well.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
